page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 physical cores with 16 vCPUs, operating at 1.0 thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance divergence between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories, respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression is also poor, ranking in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core execution is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores all achieving average ratings in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also consistently register in the average range, though the PassMark memory score is weak.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the lack of local storage, this instance is positioned for compute-focused workloads that scale across multiple threads rather than relying on single-core speed. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, static web serving, and database operations, which all perform in the average tier. It also supports light language model inference for small models, though performance degrades on medium models. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable multi-core execution, though the older Intel Xeon architecture presents a tradeoff in single-threaded efficiency compared to newer hardware classes.

It is suited for static web serving, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and small-scale language model inference.
